annotation.title_clean: Commission Decision of 5 February 2014 on the safety requirements to be met by European standards for consumer laser products pursuant to Directive 2001/95/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on general product safety (2014/59/EU)
annotation.title_en: Commission Decision of 5 February 2014 on the safety requirements to be met by European standards for consumer laser products pursuant to Directive 2001/95/EC on general product safety (2014/59/EU)
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 36/20
annotation.summary_en: European Commission Decision 2014/59/EU setting the safety requirements that European standards for consumer laser products, such as laser pointers, must meet under the General Product Safety Directive. It says these products must not damage the eyes or skin, that child-appealing products need extra protection, and that safety must be achieved by technical means. It has no AI or robotics content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines consumer laser product, child-appealing consumer laser product, and damage to the eyes or skin
Child-appealing laser products must not damage the eyes or skin under any conditions of use
Other consumer laser products must not cause eye damage or unintended skin damage under reasonably foreseeable use
Conformity must be achieved by technical means, with warning labels and instructions for residual risks
Gives the basis for asking European standardisation bodies to revise EN 60825-1
